blocks.x: October is upon us once again. The days have grown shorter and a touch cooler, and so it’s time to snuggle up with a warm mug of cider and retreat to the cozy confines of nostalgia, when we were younger, responsibilities were just a big word parents used, and every long shadow felt like a wee little goblin might pop out of it. (With the climate the way it is, it’s getting harder and harder to pretend the first half of autumn isn’t just Summer 2: Orange Summer.) And presently, there are few things that excuse a retreat from our grown-up lives more appealingly than this Halloween-themed playlist posted on the official YouTube channel for Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood.

Titled “Halloween Comfort”, the playlist features “from the vault” offerings from the universally beloved children’s series, including full episodes, compilations, and clips that complement the Samhain season. “Everything from spiders and witches to dress-up and not-so-scary monsters is introduced and explained with Mister Rogers’ legendary kind and reassuring approach,” the press release said. This is a real “gem among gems” situation: Among its videos, which will be staggered out all October long, are such highlights as “Playing Pretend with Margaret Hamilton,” an episode-long visit with the Wicked Witch Of The West herself, who addresses the frightening aspect of her Wizard Of Oz character by encouraging children to act out their fears with dress-up. Before she donned her iconic black hat, Hamilton shared fun anecdotes about her time on the Oz set (a little girl helped her eat lunch because her hands were painted green), and spoke about understanding the motivations of the Wicked Witch.

“Sometimes we think she’s just mean and a very bad person,” she informed Mister Rogers, “but actually you have to think about her point of view—that it wasn’t as happy a time as she wanted it to be because she just never got what she wanted.” (Unfortunately, Mister Rogers’ lesson in ruby-slipper jealousy was covered in another episode.) Soon, Hamilton dons her costume (but not before Mister Rogers tries on the Witch’s hat, which is fun) in a light bit of scary make-believe that drives home the episode’s theme of confronting one’s fears with play. (One wonderful bit: Mister Rogers noting that the zipper on Hamilton’s Witch costume is just like the zipper on his cardigan.) You can watch the episode in full below.

For horror enthusiasts, the YouTube channel has recently uploaded “Mister Rogers Gets A Tonsillectomy” (called “Mister Rogers Gets His Tonsils Taken Out” in the playlist), a documentary segment directed by Night Of The Living Dead maestro George A. Romero, who, like many working filmmakers in Pittsburgh in the late Sixties/early Seventies, was hired to shoot a handful of segments for the show. The previously rarely seen segment was found by Romero historian Lawrence DeVincentz and posted in full by Bloody Disgusting in 2017. “It was shot in a real, working hospital,” the director later reflected. “I had to quickly, and quietly, use my pin-lights to get exposure in the waiting room, in Fred’s bedroom, and in the O.R. I still joke that ‘Mister Rogers Gets A Tonsillectomy’ is the scariest film I’ve ever made. What I really mean is that I was scared shitless while I was trying to pull it off.”

Honestly, watching Fred Rogers being put under for minor surgery is pretty unnerving. Having to run lights and camera while doctors performed the procedure? Oh yes. Professional nightmare fuel. You can watch the Romero segment, and the very nice episode around it, in the video below.
